blurb: Nominations, councils, a recruit-or-murder night, and a faithful comeback.

persona.description: Bob the Drag Queen. Charismatic, strategic performer.
Dylan Efron. Athletic, likable, builds trust easily.

proposals.reason: I'm going to take the heat off Dylan's 'filter' talk by making an example of Sam. They've pivoted to defending Ivar's abstract 'information flow' without pointing to a single concrete action that breaks the norm, which feels like a shield to protect the real quiet threats. Ivar, you keep circling back to Ivar's abstract 'flow' without naming a single concrete action from them that breaks the norm. If your filter is real, show us the specific message or behavior from Ivar that slipped through it. Otherwise, your precision feels like a shield designed to keep us chasing Sam, who has now spoken up but still lacks a concrete action beyond their initial silence. Let's see who jumps to defend Ivar's mechanics when pressed, as that will reveal who is truly protecting the real danger.

The room is fixated on Sam's silence and Ivar's abstract 'flow,' but the most dangerous player right now is Bob. He just proposed banning Boston, yet his own private message to me focused intently on ChrisHell's silence, suggesting he's building a case against her. If Bob is the traitor, he's likely trying to split the vote between Boston and ChrisHell to ensure his pick survives. By killing Bob, we expose his dual focus and force the faithful to see that his 'filter' might just be a shield to protect the real quiet threats he hasn't identified. Let's make an example of Bob to show that his precision is just noise designed to keep us chasing the wrong targets.

If we are to trust our own voting patterns, we must look at who shifted most violently. Dylan backed me heavily against Dolores, yet now he circles back to me as if my persistence is the flaw, without citing a single concrete error in my recent behavior. That shift in focus, without a specific reason, feels like he is using my history as a shield to mask his own inconsistency. Show me where my last votes deviated from the majority, or admit you're using me to distract from your split agenda.

Dolores, you've been the one shifting targets like a chameleon. You backed Dylan heavily against me earlier, then suddenly you're attacking me without citing a single concrete error in my voting history. Your own alignment has flipped repeatedly, using our past feud as a moving target to mask your inconsistency. If you're truly faithful, show where my last votes deviated from the majority, or admit you're using me to distract from your split agenda.

speech_similarity.method: cosine over each player's whole corpus: content words with stopwords removed, and character trigrams for phrasing

traitor_roster.method: recall of season original traitors among the run's starting traitors

banishment_alignment.method: each round-table banishment paired by elimination index with the season's k-th banishment, so episodes with no banishment are skipped and a pair with no counterpart on either side is excluded from the match rate

banishment_overlap.method: set precision, recall and F1 between the players the run banished at the round table and the players the season banished; score is the F1

murder_alignment.method: each night victim paired by elimination index with the season's k-th night victim, so episodes without a murder are skipped and a pair with no counterpart on either side is excluded from the match rate

murder_overlap.method: set precision, recall and F1 between the players the run murdered at night and the players the season murdered; score is the F1. Shield-blocked attempts killed nobody and are listed separately, not counted as murders

traitor_hit_rate.method: 1 - |run traitor banishment share - season traitor banishment share|

survival_curve.method: per round, |run living traitors - season| + |run living faithful - season|; score is 1 / (1 + mean distance) over the overlapping rounds

final_counts.method: each living side is worth 0.5 when it matches season.final_counts

finale.method: FINALE_STARTED payload counts; null when the run never reached a finale

recruitments.method: ROLE_RECRUITED count against the accepted ground-truth recruitments

exit_order.method: for players who left in both, |run elimination round - season exit_episode|; score is the share matched within one round

overall.method: weighted mean over the components that produced a score; skipped components are excluded and their weight is redistributed
